stories.label: VIP-экстрадиция: Кыргызстан возвращает критиков власти в страну на частных самолетах. Перелеты стоят миллионы сомов
stories.summary: A joint Kloop and Temirov Live investigation finds Kyrgyz authorities have made a routine of detaining critics abroad, flying them home and prosecuting them, and at least two of these extraditions used chartered private jets costing roughly 10 million som. Lead with the private jets and their price: public money spent to bring dissidents back. Name who was returned, from which countries, and which agencies arranged the flights; the structural point is transnational repression by a Central Asian state with the cooperation of host governments.

stories.label: The Syrians Languishing in Israel’s Prisons
stories.summary: Israeli forces operating in southern Syria have detained dozens of Syrians, some of them teenage boys taken from farms and family homes, and their families do not know where they are held or why. Lead with a named detainee and the family's search. The mechanism: Israel's occupation of a buffer zone inside Syria has produced detention without charge or notification, with no channel for families or the Syrian state to get answers. Give the number held and the legal basis Israel claims, if any.

stories.label: St. Catherine Monastery’s land ownership lawsuits adjourned after archbishop backs Egypt-Greece deal
stories.summary: The archbishop of St. Catherine's Monastery in Sinai says he will sign an agreement with the Egyptian government that, under Cairo's July draft, consolidates ownership of the monastery and surrounding lands in the Egyptian state, and the land lawsuits have been adjourned. Lead with the transfer: a community on that land for 1,400 years cedes title to the state. Explain what the Egypt-Greece deal gives each side, why the courts paused, and how it fits Cairo's wider development plans for the South Sinai area.

stories.label: Anthropic's IPO filing shows explosive growth, risks and staggering costs
stories.summary: Anthropic's public S-1 shows first-half 2026 revenue of $16.3 billion against a net loss of $80.7 billion, ahead of a November Nasdaq listing under ANT. Lead with that ratio: five dollars lost for every dollar earned. The mechanism is compute spending, so show where the losses go and what the risk factors disclose about cloud and chip dependence. Context: it lands as Meta raises $95bn and Elon Musk warns smaller AI firms face collapse.

stories.label: Meta plans $95bn stock offering to help cover AI expansion
stories.summary: Meta announced a two-part $95 billion equity raise, common and preferred stock, to fund data centres, the largest such raise by a tech company, on the same day Elon Musk warned hundreds of AI startups face collapse as funding dries up. Lead with the shift: a company that funded AI from cash flow now needs shareholders' money, diluting them. Explain why equity rather than debt, and where the capital goes (Nvidia and AMD chips, data centres).

stories.label: Lucky Group, Qatar Energy consortium quits Port Qasim LNG terminal plan over 'policy changes'
stories.summary: Energas, a consortium of Pakistan's Lucky Group and QatarEnergy, has abandoned its planned LNG terminal at Port Qasim, citing changes to Pakistan's energy policy and unresolved fiscal matters. Lead with what Pakistan loses: import capacity for natural gas while the Hormuz crisis squeezes Gulf supply. Name the policy changes the consortium blames and who in Islamabad made them; the structural point is investor flight from Pakistan's energy sector.

stories.label: Brazil's markets set to tumble as investors bet Lula will add to fiscal pain
stories.summary: New development on Lula's win, already covered: the market verdict. Brazil's real and stocks fell on Monday after investors positioned for a Flávio Bolsonaro victory bet that Lula will widen the budget deficit. Lead with the size of the moves in the real and the Bovespa and the US dollar rate. Explain the mechanism: higher deficits mean higher interest rates from the central bank, and who pays for that, from borrowers to the poor Lula's programmes serve.

stories.label: Iraq’s Fuel Crisis Exposes Its Oil Dependence
stories.summary: The closure of the Strait of Hormuz has left Iraq, one of the world's largest crude exporters, short of fuel at home and squeezed fiscally, because it exports crude through the Gulf and imports refined fuel back. Lead with the paradox: an oil state with fuel queues. Tie it to Brent crude and ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, and name who bears it: households, generators and power cuts. The structural why: decades of war, corruption and stalled refinery reform.

stories.label: Satellites show some of the strongest evidence the AMOC is weakening | New Scientist
stories.summary: Satellite measurements of the heat the North Atlantic releases to the atmosphere suggest the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation has slowed 18 per cent in 40 years, a direct observational line where earlier evidence leaned on models and proxies. Lead with the 18 per cent. Explain the method, why heat release tracks the current, and what a weaker AMOC means beyond Europe: shifted monsoons over West Africa and South Asia. Name the journal and authors.

stories.label: A virus that afflicts cows makes the jump to a human
stories.summary: STAT reports a virus known in cattle has been found infecting a human. Lead with the virus, where the case was found and how it was detected; then the mechanism: what spillover from livestock requires, whether there is any sign of human-to-human spread, and what surveillance in dairy and cattle herds does and does not catch. Report only the lead item in the newsletter; ignore the other news it rounds up.

stories.label: Popular AI tool LiteLLM says unrevoked key allowed hackers to target users
stories.summary: LiteLLM, the open-source gateway many developers use to route calls to AI models, says a key accidentally exposed in May and never revoked let attackers mount last week's supply-chain attack, believed to have hit tens of thousands of users. Lead with the five months the key stayed live. The mechanism: one credential in a widely used package gave access to every downstream install, and a gateway holds the API keys for every model it routes to. Say what users should rotate.

stories.label: AI models cost more when you don’t use English
stories.summary: Tokenizers built mostly on English text split other languages into far more tokens, so speakers of Arabic, Urdu, Bengali, Amharic and others pay more per sentence and get less usable context from the same model. Lead with the multiplier for the worst-served language against English. Explain the mechanism (byte-pair encoding trained on English-heavy data), who sets the price, and what labs or regional models are doing about it.

stories.label: 端到端推理时延降低 15%：京东广告联合鲲鹏超节点，探索生成式广告行业新路径
stories.summary: JD.com's ad business says generative recommendation needs a thousand times more compute within a 300-millisecond budget, and that the bottleneck is general-purpose CPU and memory, not GPUs. Working with Huawei's Kunpeng supernode, it cut four cache tiers to two over a 300TB shared memory pool and cut end-to-end inference latency 15%, tested on 5% of traffic in the 618 sale. Lead with the claim that the constraint is not the GPU: a Chinese platform working around export controls with domestic hardware. Note this is the companies' own account.

stories.label: Report: IDF chief warned U.S. that striking Iran would disrupt Israel's election
stories.summary: New development on the eve of Tuesday's Israeli vote: CNN reports IDF chief Eyal Zamir warned his US counterpart that a joint strike on Iran would disrupt the election, as Netanyahu pressed Washington to strike before polling day; Defence Minister Katz denies any such 'intention', and opposition leader Avigdor Lieberman now demands a criminal investigation into Netanyahu for pressuring security chiefs toward confrontation with Tehran. Lead with the army chief resisting his own prime minister: the mechanism is a war timed to an election, and the people who would bear it are Iranians and the Gulf states downrange. Dateline Tel Aviv.

stories.label: India's Opposition Leader Gandhi Acquitted in Defamation Case
stories.summary: A trial court in Sultanpur acquitted Rahul Gandhi of criminal defamation over remarks about Home Minister Amit Shah, ending an eight-year case. Lead with the eight years: the mechanism is criminal defamation — a law that can jail, and in 2023 briefly cost Gandhi his parliamentary seat — used as a standing tool against India's opposition leader. Dateline Sultanpur.

stories.label: Japan Indicts US Marine Over Okinawa Killing, Media Say
stories.summary: Japanese prosecutors indicted Lance Corporal Devin Jacob Ballard of Marine Corps Air Station Futenma for the robbery and murder of a Japanese woman in Okinawa. Lead with the charge, then the structure: Okinawa hosts most of the US forces in Japan, and the Status of Forces Agreement shapes when Japan can take custody of a service member — the reason each such crime becomes a question of sovereignty. Dateline Naha.

stories.label: Deadly Ukrainian drone attack hits Russia's Voronezh region
stories.summary: Two people were killed and 17 injured, a child among them, in a Ukrainian drone attack on Russia's Voronezh region, the governor said, as both sides traded overnight strikes. Lead with the toll, counted the same way civilians in Ukraine are counted; the context is that strikes deep into each country continue while the Kremlin talks of trilateral negotiations in November. Casualty figures come from the Russian regional governor and TASS: attribute them. Dateline Voronezh.

stories.label: Germany's Business Outlook Unexpectedly Improves for Sixth Month
stories.summary: The Ifo expectations index rose to 91.6 in October from 90.4, a sixth straight gain economists did not forecast, even with Brent crude above $100 on the Iran war. Lead with the surprise: Europe's biggest economy is recovering through an energy shock. Second beat: the wider euro zone is slowing, which is why the ECB is expected to hold rates on Thursday — name the euro and the ECB rate. Dateline Munich.

stories.label: Federal Reserve expected to tap brakes on rate hikes
stories.summary: The Fed under Kevin Warsh is expected to hold rates on Wednesday, a week before the midterms, and then raise them again in December. Lead with the pause in a hiking cycle and the political pressure behind it: Trump allies urged no hike before the vote. The mechanism is war-driven oil inflation meeting an election calendar; name the Fed funds rate, US inflation and the US 10-year Treasury yield, and that the ECB and Bank of Japan also decide this week. Dateline Washington.

stories.label: JI threatens march to Islamabad in mid-November if petroleum levy not abolished
stories.summary: Jamaat-i-Islami's emir Hafiz Naeemur Rehman says the party will march on Islamabad in mid-November unless PM Shehbaz Sharif scraps the petroleum levy, Rs114 a litre on petrol. Lead with who pays: with Brent crude above $100 on the Iran war, the levy — a revenue line Pakistan leans on under its IMF programme — lands on every commuter and farmer. The mechanism is a state balancing its budget at the pump. Dateline Lahore.

stories.label: Bitcoin wallet bug let rogue servers steal funds when users tried to speed up payments
stories.summary: A flaw in Electrum, one of the oldest bitcoin wallets, let malicious servers trick users into signing payments to attackers when they tried to speed up a stuck transaction (fee bumping). Lead with the trigger: the routine act of raising a fee was the attack surface. The mechanism is trust in third-party servers — users on their own or trusted servers were not exposed — and the fix is to upgrade and verify addresses before signing.

stories.label: Unitree’s newly launched H2-X Robot loses a leg in public demonstration
stories.summary: A day after its unveiling, Unitree's H2-X humanoid lost a lower leg when it fell landing a side flip at the World Physical AI Conference in Hangzhou. Lead with the failure on stage, then what it shows: China's humanoid makers sell on acrobatic demos, and a part breaking off under the load of a landing is a test of durability that those demos rarely report. Dateline Hangzhou.

stories.label: Over 11 million BTC can't be linked to any known owner
stories.summary: Even after years of ETF and corporate buying, on-chain analysts cannot tie more than 11 million bitcoin — over half the supply — to any known owner. Lead with the share: a fully public ledger still hides who owns most of it, a mix of lost coins, unidentified institutions and layered custody. Note bitcoin itself has slipped below $80,000 on the AI selloff ahead of the Fed; name bitcoin as the series.

stories.label: Neoadjuvant durvalumab plus chemotherapy in resectable or borderline resectable non-small-cell lung cancer: the phase 2 MDT-BRIDGE trial - Nature Medicine
stories.summary: A phase 2 trial in Nature Medicine tested durvalumab immunotherapy plus chemotherapy before surgery in lung cancer judged borderline operable — patients usually outside the phase 3 trials. Lead with the result for that group: how many could then be operated on and how tumours responded. The mechanism is shrinking a tumour enough to make surgery possible. Report the trial size and phase plainly; it is not a practice-changing phase 3.

stories.label: Saudi Civil Defence Lifts Safety Alerts After Missile Threat Passes
stories.summary: Saudi forces intercepted about 10 Houthi ballistic missiles, falling debris injured two, alerts sounded in Makkah, Jeddah and Taif, and the coalition says it destroyed two launchers in Sanaa in reply. The Houthis claim they hit pumping stations on the East-West pipeline, Riyadh's route for exporting crude that avoids the Strait of Hormuz; Saudi Arabia has not confirmed it. That claim is the stake: name the pipeline and Brent crude, and say plainly that the hit is unverified. This advances the watched Houthi-threat arc from threats on Riyadh airport to missiles fired.

stories.label: Europe's growing support for Ukraine earns it larger role in upcoming negotiations, Kremlin says
stories.summary: A reversal: Putin's aide Yuri Ushakov now says Europe should have a seat in the US-Ukraine-Russia talks, because Washington's leverage over Kyiv has shrunk while Europe pays more of the war's cost. The same day Zelensky said the trilateral talks are expected in November, and the Kremlin said preparations for a Putin-Xi-Trump summit have begun. Lead with Moscow asking for the Europeans it spent years shutting out, and explain who now holds leverage over the terms.

stories.label: Uganda orders 21-day Ebola quarantine for citizens returning from DR Congo
stories.summary: Uganda now orders a 21-day quarantine for citizens coming back from the DR Congo, even as Kampala insists the country is Ebola-free and Swiss authorities say the woman diagnosed in Nigeria was most likely infected in Uganda. Lead with that contradiction: a government's interest in being declared clear runs against the tracing the region needs. Tie it to Nigeria's widening screening, which we covered, as the regional chain of the outbreak.

stories.label: Gayton McKenzie's mystery visits to Blu Label ahead of controversial Ticketpro deal
stories.summary: Daily Maverick reports that South Africa's sports minister, Gayton McKenzie, repeatedly visited JSE-listed Blu Label before it sold its Ticketpro subsidiary to a consortium linked to his own Patriotic Alliance. Lead with the visits as evidence and explain the conflict-of-interest mechanism: a minister whose department buys event ticketing, and a party-linked buyer. Accountability inside the coalition government, reported by original investigative journalism; attribute every claim to the outlet.

stories.label: Tehran to host Saudi, Turkish, Pakistani officials
stories.summary: Iranian state news agency Mehr reports, citing SNSC deputy secretary Ali Bagheri Kani, that Saudi defence minister Khalid bin Salman, Pakistan's army chief Asim Munir and Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin will meet jointly in Tehran. If it happens, the region's main Sunni military powers would be sitting in Tehran while Houthi missiles fall on Saudi cities and Washington readies strikes on Iran. Attribute it throughout as an announcement by Iranian state media that the other governments have not confirmed. The stake is whether a regional security track is forming outside the US.

stories.label: Saudi Arabia to store crude oil in Singapore to bolster Asia supply security
stories.summary: From the second half of 2027 Saudi Arabia will store crude in Singapore's Jurong Rock Caverns, an oil buffer placed on the far side of the Strait of Hormuz after the US-Israeli war with Iran choked ship traffic through it. Lead with the world's largest exporter moving supply security out of the Gulf, and name Brent crude and ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. Pair it with today's Houthi claim on the East-West pipeline, the other bypass.

stories.label: Elon Musk has a warning for AI neoclouds
stories.summary: Musk confirmed that Nasdaq-listed SpaceX raised $40 billion in debt to buy GPUs, and said debt markets have largely closed to AI cloud companies with no revenue beyond data centres. He predicts the 200-plus 'neocloud' providers will shrink to a few survivors. Lead with the $40 billion and the closing credit window. The mechanism is GPU-backed lending, and whether chips that lose value fast can carry that much debt.

stories.label: Sharp rise in prices of smartphones burdens consumers
stories.summary: In Pakistan an entry-level phone (4GB RAM, 64GB storage) now costs about Rs40,000, up from Rs22,000 a few months ago, and dealers blame chip costs rather than taxes. Lead with the near-doubling. The mechanism: AI data centres are buying up memory chips, and the cost lands on low- and middle-income buyers in the Global South, for whom a phone is the bank, the shop and the internet.

stories.label: 13亿！北京Token工厂拿下新融资
stories.summary: Beijing's Approaching.AI, an inference provider that sells AI output measured in tokens and was founded by Tsinghua HPC researchers, raised over 1.3 billion yuan in a Series B led by state-linked funds (2.4 billion this year). It claims daily output above a trillion tokens, running trillion-parameter models on domestic chips by splitting prefill and decode across mixed Chinese and foreign hardware. Lead with the inside view: China's 'token factory' boom, from Infinigence's 2.3 billion to SiliconFlow's IPO filing, is how it gets round export controls in the inference layer. The company's efficiency claims are its own.

stories.label: US says helped Gulf nations export 1.5 bn barrels of oil through Hormuz
stories.summary: CENTCOM says US forces have escorted more than 1.5 billion barrels of Gulf crude through the Strait of Hormuz since summer, past Iran's blockade, and its commander flew over the strait to declare key routes clear of mines. Lead with the figure and what it implies for ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and Brent crude; set it against Araghchi's claim (covered earlier today) that Hormuz management will never return to the pre-war order. It is a US military claim: attribute it, and note that IRGC mine strikes on tankers were reported as recently as 23 October.

stories.label: Students' List wins snap parliamentary elections in Serbia -- Vucic
stories.summary: A youth-backed Students' List, born from the mass student protests, has won Serbia's snap parliamentary election, by the account of former president Aleksandar Vucic, who called it a 'revolution' backed by European states and the 'US deep state' and predicted it will impose sanctions on Russia by spring. Lead with a protest movement taking power at the ballot box; the stakes are Serbia's long balance between Moscow and Brussels. The only source is Russian state agency TASS: attribute every claim to it ('Russian state news agency TASS reported...') and present Vucic's charges as his.

stories.label: KP Governor Kundi says Sohail Afridi, assembly speaker 'in safe hands' after house arrest
stories.summary: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's governor has acknowledged for the first time that the province's elected chief minister, Sohail Afridi, and assembly speaker Babar Saleem Swati are under house arrest. Afridi, missing from public view since Islamabad imposed governor's rule, was reported missing on 19 October. Lead with the official admission: a federally appointed governor holding the elected heads of a province's government. The mechanism is emergency rule in Imran Khan's stronghold, and the people of KP have lost their elected government.

stories.label: Ebola: NCDC expands health declaration requirement for international travellers
stories.summary: Nigeria's disease-control agency now requires health declarations from more international travellers and has instructed the airport and aviation authorities to enforce them with airlines. This advances the Bundibugyo Ebola arc covered on 24 October (Lagos emergency response) with a decision at the border. Lead with who must declare and how it is enforced. Bundibugyo has no licensed vaccine, which is why border screening is one of the few tools left.

stories.label: Iran, Russia gas agreement near finalization: Acting oil min.
stories.summary: Iran's caretaker oil minister, Hamid Bovard, says the broad agreements on a gas exchange with Russia are in their final stages, building on the 2024 Gazprom–NIGC memorandum. Lead with what a Russian gas swap gives Iran while its Gulf exports run through a war zone: a sanctioned supplier tying itself to another, and the hold Moscow gains over a wartime Tehran. Natural gas is the series to chart. The only source is Iranian state outlet Mehr, so attribute the claim and do not state the deal as done.

stories.label: Enough golfers commit to LIV 2.0 to keep hopes of new league alive
stories.summary: About 15 golfers have tentatively signed on to a private-equity-backed successor to LIV Golf, ahead of a Friday deadline set by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund. Lead with the PIF moving the bill for its flagship sports project onto outside investors, and with the bankruptcy questions over the original league. The structural story is a sovereign wealth fund, stretched by a Gulf war and oil exports through Hormuz, pulling back from soft-power spending. Say who is paying and who is leaving.

stories.label: Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro face off over competing visions of Brazil’s future
stories.summary: Brazilians vote today in the presidential runoff: Flávio Bolsonaro led the first round 47.03% to Lula's 45.16%, a 1.9-point gap. New development since our Telegram-disinformation piece: the vote itself. Lead with the stakes beyond Brazil: it is the last big test of Latin America's rightward swing, and the two men offer opposite foreign policies, including on Israel and Palestine (Mondoweiss). Dateline Brasília.

stories.label: Death toll from Israeli bombardments across Gaza rises to seven
stories.summary: Israel struck the Islamic University in Gaza City twice, killing three security guards, and at least seven Palestinians died across the Strip despite the ceasefire. Lead with the university campus as a target: the strip's higher-education infrastructure is still being hit during a declared truce. Name the dead where the sources do, and state who carried out the strikes.

stories.label: Machado returns to Venezuela after 10 months of exile
stories.summary: New development on the Venezuela arc (protests demanding an election date were covered today): Nobel laureate María Corina Machado is back in the country after 10 months in exile. Lead with the return and the risk she now runs under Maduro's government; explain how it collides with the street demand for a presidential election date and what Caracas has said about arresting her.

stories.label: Netanyahu publishes AI image of nuclear strike on Tel Aviv, warning of 'second Holocaust' by Iran
stories.summary: Two days before Israel's election, the sitting prime minister posted an AI-generated image of a nuclear blast over Tel Aviv, saying a rival 'incapable of confronting Iran' would invite a 'second Holocaust'. Lead with a head of government campaigning with synthetic imagery of his own city's destruction; the mechanism is fear of Iran as the closing electoral argument while the Gulf war continues, against Eisenkot.

stories.label: Be cautious, Filipinos in Spain told amid unrest
stories.summary: A student protest against 'the system' in Barcelona turned into looting and clashes, with more than 100 arrested and dozens of shops damaged, a day after France's mass protests. Lead with the arrest count and the spread: youth cost-of-living protests organised on social media are now hitting a second EU state. Datelined Barcelona; France was covered yesterday and is context only.

stories.label: Organizations rally in support of Mada Masr, condemn ‘weaponization’ of media law against independent journalism
stories.summary: Egyptian prosecutors have referred Mada Masr editor-in-chief Lina Attalah to trial, the step beyond the near-annual questioning the outlet has faced. Lead with the referral and the law used against her; the mechanism is a media law turned into a tool against Egypt's last major independent newsroom. Note the domestic and international bodies now backing her.

stories.label: Intensive int'l and UN efforts to end Sudan war
stories.summary: A Geneva meeting of 21 countries set out concrete confidence-building steps for Sudan: prisoner exchanges and coordination so students can sit secondary-school exams across front lines, toward a humanitarian truce. Lead with the exams detail — a war that has split a country's school system — and name who is at the table and who (SAF, RSF) must agree.

stories.label: Faltou ônibus em Salvador no 2º turno, oito dias após Câmara dar título a Flávio Bolsonaro
stories.summary: New development on today's runoff: in Salvador, a Lula stronghold, the bus fleet was held back on voting day and voters were left on foot; the electoral court (TRE) ordered the arrest of the responsible municipal secretary, who is in Paris. Lead with the arrest order; the mechanism is transport denial as voter suppression, eight days after the city council honoured Flávio Bolsonaro.

stories.label: Iliana Iotova winning first round of presidential election in Bulgaria -- exit poll
stories.summary: New development on the Bulgaria arc (the pre-vote story ran today): exit polls put incumbent Iliana Iotova first with 35.3%, ahead of opposition-backed Andrey Gyurov, pointing to a runoff. Source is Russian state news agency TASS only — attribute the figures to it. Explain what a runoff between them means for Bulgaria's Black Sea and Ukraine stance.

stories.label: Hormuz management to never return to pre-war era: Araghchi
stories.summary: Beyond yesterday's reopening offer: Foreign Minister Araghchi says the Strait of Hormuz will be managed differently after the war, not as before, while speaker Qalibaf threatens an 'unimaginable' response to any US move. Lead with Iran claiming a permanent say over the strait; the mechanism is a war turning a free passage into a managed one. Tie it to ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and Brent crude.

stories.label: Uneven petrol prices, lingering hardship as Zaria residents question NNPC discount
stories.summary: The federal government announced a petrol price cut at NNPC stations, but in Zaria, Kaduna State, drivers and tricycle operators say pump prices are uneven and they see no relief. Lead with the gap between the announced discount and the pump; explain why it does not pass through (private marketers, supply) while war-driven crude prices and a weak naira squeeze households.

stories.label: America has lost 200k of jobs in media, film and the arts. How much is AI?
stories.summary: US employment in media, film and the arts has fallen by about 200,000 jobs; the Apricitas analysis separates how much of that is generative AI versus streaming retrenchment and the post-strike slump. Lead with the 200k figure and what the data does and does not attribute to AI — the reader wants the mechanism, not the hype. Tie to US jobs data.

stories.label: Latvia targets tokenization rules in 2027 with commercial property in focus
stories.summary: Latvia aims to have rules for tokenising real-world assets by mid-2027, starting with commercial property, but the legal assessment due 1 October is still unfinished and the minister driving it lost his party's seats in this month's election. Lead with the stall: an EU state's blockchain property plan hostage to a change of government.

stories.label: At ESMO, AstraZeneca's cancer pursuits get a showcase
stories.summary: Trial data presented at the ESMO oncology congress in Madrid on AstraZeneca's antibody-drug conjugates in lung and gastric cancer. Lead with the strongest survival result and what it changes for patients; gastric cancer weighs heavily in Asia, so note who gets access and at what price.

stories.label: UK's Rayner Defends Burnham Move to Revisit EU Free Movement
stories.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham has opened the question Brexit was meant to close: a return to EU free movement, while ruling out the euro and Schengen. Lead with the precedent — the first sitting UK leader since 2016 to put free movement on the table — and the mechanism: what Brussels would demand in return for single-market access, and who gains (workers, students, firms short of labour). Rayner defending it signals cabinet backing.

stories.label: Who is B.C.'s new premier Lorne Doerkson?
stories.summary: British Columbia's Conservatives won a provincial election for the first time in nearly a century, beating NDP premier David Eby in a snap vote he called himself. Lead with the backfire — a leader who chose the timing and lost — then what moved voters (cost of living, housing, resources) and what a Conservative government means for the province's pipelines, LNG exports and Indigenous land agreements. Dateline Victoria.

stories.label: Amit Shah Slams Congress Over Kharge's 'Modi Ka Baap Bhi Jayega' Remark
stories.summary: Congress president Kharge, campaigning in Patna, accused Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar of facilitating large-scale 'vote theft' for the BJP and demanded his removal. Lead with the institution, not the insult: the opposition is now attacking the referee of the world's largest electorate during the Bihar campaign. Explain what evidence underlies the 'vote chori' charge (voter-roll revisions) and how the CEC is appointed — a panel the government controls.

stories.label: CENTCOM reportedly has plans for Iran strikes: Will Trump approve them?
stories.summary: The Pentagon has reportedly drawn up options to renew strikes on Iran after the 3 November US midterms (first reported by The Hill). Lead with the timing — war plans parked until after an election — and the question analysts raise: what a second bombing campaign achieves that the first did not, while Iran offers to reopen Hormuz against the US blockade. Who bears the cost: Iranian civilians and Gulf shipping. Attribute the plans clearly as reported, not confirmed.

stories.label: Aref asks Azeri girls facing bans to continue studies in Iran
stories.summary: Iran's first vice president invited Azerbaijani schoolgirls and women barred over the hijab to study at Iranian universities, after Iran's science ministry offered places. Lead with who is affected: Muslim girls in a Muslim-majority country losing access to education over a headscarf. Explain Azerbaijan's restriction and the Baku–Tehran rivalry behind the offer. State media only: attribute to Iran's Mehr news agency and do not state the scale of the ban as fact.

stories.label: IndiGo, Air India to shift flights to Navi Mumbai airport from Dec
stories.summary: India's two dominant airlines will move flights, including 38 international routes, from Mumbai's main airport to the new Adani-run Navi Mumbai airport from December, as Terminal 1 is rebuilt. Lead with the concentration: both Mumbai airports now sit with the Adani Group, which runs a large share of India's airport traffic, and two carriers hold most of the market. Who pays: passengers facing longer transfers and one operator setting charges.

stories.label: Hong Kong seeks bigger role for yuan in regional trade, treasury chief says
stories.summary: Hong Kong's treasury chief Christopher Hui pressed finance ministers at last week's Apec meeting, including Brunei's, to settle regional trade in the yuan. Lead with the mechanism: Hong Kong as the offshore clearing hub that lets Asian and Muslim-world economies invoice outside the dollar, at a time when US sanctions and the Gulf war make dollar dependence a risk. Name the yuan as the series to chart.

stories.label: Russia prepared to export as much of diesel fuel as US may need -- deputy PM
stories.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak says Russia will ship the US 'as much diesel as needed' under a diesel deal between the two countries — a sanctioned exporter now supplying the sanctioning power, as the Hormuz closure squeezes fuel markets. Lead with that reversal and what it means for Brent crude and for Europe, which banned Russian diesel. State media only: write 'Russian state news agency TASS reported' and establish the deal's terms only as far as the source supports.

stories.label: 何伟文：AI投资勃兴驱动中国和世界贸易剧增 | 巴伦独家
stories.summary: Chinese trade economist He Weiwen argues the boom in AI-related goods — servers, chips, power equipment — is driving China's export growth, rewriting the 'overcapacity' story told about China's trade surplus. The inside view from Beijing: lead with the trade figures on AI hardware, and present the overcapacity rebuttal as his argument, attributed. It is the mirror of Apollo's finding that AI's payoff has not reached buyers.

stories.label: UK banks hit by 10,000 crypto transfer complaints
stories.summary: UK banks drew 10,000 complaints in three months over blocking or capping transfers to crypto exchanges, even regulated ones. Lead with the contradiction: a government courting crypto firms while its banks quietly cut customers off through blanket bans and opaque limits. Mechanism: banks pass fraud liability onto payment blocks. Bitcoin is the series to chart.
